Additionally, the absence of shared downstream molecular pathways between prion protein aggregation and CACNB4 dysfunction would weaken this link. _(variant: gnomAD analysis revealing common variants in PRNP (e.g., rs1799907) or CACNB4 with frequencies significantly above expected for rare disease alleles would challenge their causal role in these rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared impact on neuronal calcium signaling could reveal therapeutic targets applicable to both prion diseases and certain forms of ataxia. Modulating calcium channel activity or downstream signaling pathways affected by both PRNP and CACNB4 dysfunction could offer novel treatment strategies for these distinct but mechanistically linked neurological disorders.
